vocabulary.meaning_en: a question word that replaces a noun we don't know: who, whom, whose, which, what

vocabulary.example: An interrogative sentence is a question.
Who told you to wait here?
To whom should I write this letter?

vocabulary.note_ar: لا تخلطها مع who's = who is
vocabulary.note_en: Don't confuse with who's (= who is).

vocabulary.meaning_en: what one (from a choice of things)
vocabulary.example: Which is better, the chocolate or the vanilla cake?

vocabulary.meaning_en: which thing (when we don't know the thing)
a person, a place or a thing
the person or thing that does the action
vocabulary.example: In "Tom likes apples", Tom is the subject.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the person or thing that receives the action
vocabulary.example: In "I called Tom", Tom is the object.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the act of choosing; something you can choose
vocabulary.example: Tea or coffee? It's your choice.
Whoever ate my chocolate must buy me more!

vocabulary.meaning_en: any one of a choice; it doesn't matter which
anything; also a rude reply meaning "I don't care"
vocabulary.note_ar: الرد Whatever! قد يكون غير مهذب
vocabulary.note_en: As a reply, "Whatever!" can be rude.
vocabulary.example: You can eat whatever you want.

fine_lines.title: who vs whom
fine_lines.explanation_ar: who للسؤال عن الشخص الفاعل (الذي يقوم بالفعل). whom للسؤال عن الشخص المفعول به (الذي يستقبل الفعل) وهي رسمية، وتأتي غالبًا بعد حرف جر: to whom.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Who" asks about the person who does the action (subject). "Whom" asks about the person who receives it (object); it is formal and often follows a preposition: to whom.

examples.sentence: To whom did you send the letter?

fine_lines.title: whose vs who's
fine_lines.explanation_ar: whose = لمن (ملكية). who's = who is أو who has. تُنطقان بالطريقة نفسها.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Whose" = belonging to whom. "Who's" = who is / who has. They sound the same.

fine_lines.title: which vs what
fine_lines.explanation_ar: which عندما نختار من خيارات محددة معروفة. what عندما لا نعرف الشيء أو الخيارات مفتوحة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Which" when we choose from known options. "What" when we don't know the thing or the options are open.

examples.sentence: Which do you want, red or green?

expressions.meaning_en: A formal start for a letter when you don't know the reader's name.
expressions.example: To whom it may concern, I am writing to ask about the job.

expressions.meaning_en: Who do these things belong to?
expressions.example: I found some keys. Whose are these?

expressions.meaning_en: Asking about a thing you don't know.
expressions.example: What is this? It's a flashlight.
We have tea or juice. Which option would you like?

grammar.title: Nouns: person, place, thing
grammar.explanation_ar: الاسم شخص أو مكان أو شيء. الأشياء تشمل الأغراض والحيوانات والأفكار (مثل economics). في الثقافة الغربية قد يُعامل الحيوان الأليف كأنه شخص.
grammar.explanation_en: A noun is a person, a place or a thing. Things include objects, animals and ideas (like economics). In Western culture, a pet is often treated like a person.
examples: thing: a ball, a cat, an idea

grammar.title: Interrogative pronouns replace unknown nouns
grammar.explanation_ar: عندما لا نعرف الاسم نسأل عنه بضمير استفهام يحل محله: Tom likes apples → Who likes apples?
grammar.explanation_en: When we don't know a noun, we ask with an interrogative pronoun that takes its place: Tom likes apples → Who likes apples?
examples: Somebody told you to wait. → Who told you to wait?
Something is wrong. → What is wrong?

grammar.title: For people: who (subject), whom (object), whose (possession)
grammar.explanation_ar: للأشخاص ثلاث كلمات: who للفاعل، whom للمفعول به (رسمية)، whose للملكية.
grammar.explanation_en: For people, there are three words: who (subject), whom (object, formal), whose (possession).
examples: Who told you to wait here?
To whom should I write this letter?

grammar.title: For things: which (choice) and what (unknown)
grammar.explanation_ar: which للاختيار بين أشياء، و what لشيء لا نعرفه. وكلاهما يمكن أن يكون فاعلًا أو مفعولًا.
grammar.explanation_en: "Which" for a choice between things; "what" for a thing we don't know. Both can be subject or object.
examples: Which is better, chocolate or vanilla?

grammar.title: Bonus: add -ever for emphasis
grammar.explanation_ar: نضيف ever لهذه الكلمات للتوكيد أو الدهشة: whoever, whomever, whichever, whatever. والرد Whatever! يعني "لا يهمني" وقد يكون غير مهذب.
grammar.explanation_en: Add "-ever" for emphasis or surprise: whoever, whomever, whichever, whatever. The reply "Whatever!" means "I don't care" and can be rude.
examples: Whoever ate my chocolate must say sorry!
We'll finish it, whichever way we have to do it.

questions.question: "___ told you to wait here?" (subject, a person)
questions.explanation_en: Asking about the person who did it (subject): who.

questions.question: "To ___ should I write this letter?"
questions.explanation_ar: الشخص يستقبل الرسالة (مفعول) وبعد حرف جر: whom.
questions.explanation_en: The person receives the letter (object), after "to": whom.

questions.question: "___ is better, the chocolate or the vanilla cake?"
questions.explanation_en: A choice between two things: which.

questions.question: "___ did I do wrong?"
questions.explanation_ar: سؤال عن شيء غير معروف: what.
questions.explanation_en: Asking about an unknown thing: what.

questions.question: Which phrase is used at the start of a formal letter?
questions.explanation_ar: التعبير الرسمي: To whom it may concern.
questions.explanation_en: The formal phrase is "To whom it may concern".

questions.question: A noun is ___.
questions.explanation_ar: الاسم شخص أو مكان أو شيء.
questions.explanation_en: A noun is a person, place or thing.

questions.question: "___ ate my chocolate must buy me more!" (emphasis: any person)
